title: Kernel marketplace + bandit autotuner leveraging sequence-length histograms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, production-safe kernel selection subsystem that treats available kernel implementations as a "marketplace" and continuously selects the best kernel per model+seqlen profile using online signals. Motivation: current static heuristics struggle with mixed workloads (short chat turns + long context generations) and heterogeneous fleets (A100/H100 mixed). We want an autotuner that minimizes p95 latency regressions while improving cost-per-token across typical Redwood workloads.

Scope and constraints:
- Do not add blocking RPCs in the hot path; all selection decisions must be usable with a cheap in-memory routing table.
- Each candidate kernel implementation must expose a micro-benchmarkable fingerprint (memory occupancy, expected throughput at N tokens, and prefill/decode-mode preference).
- Safe exploration: use a constrained multi-armed bandit with enforced latency guardrails (reject any kernel that exceeds baseline p95 threshold for 5 consecutive windows).
- Must work with prefill + decode scheduling: selection can differ between prefill and decode phases (e.g., blockwise attention kernels for prefill, tiled kernels for decode).
- Runtime must be able to fall back to a stable generic kernel when metrics are noisy or hardware reporting is absent.

Deliverables:
1) Kernel marketplace registry (in-memory + persisted snapshot) with metadata and micro-benchmark results.
2) Online bandit-based tuner that consumes sequence-length histograms per model and runtime telemetry to bias exploration.
3) Prefill/decode routing policy that accepts per-request seqlen estimate and returns selected kernel + reason.
4) Integration tests and a dashboard to surface p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, and exploration rate.

Success metrics:
- 5-10% reduction in cost-per-token for mixed-seqlen workloads in experimental cluster (measured over 7 days).
- No >5% regressions in p95 latency for any production route during rollout.
- Telemetry noise reduced through histogram bucketing and 60s aggregation windows.

Related artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Kernel+Marketplace+Design (proto draft)
- Microbench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/microbench/tree/feature/marketplace
- Dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/kernel-marketplace
- Spike PR (benchmarks + small bandit impl): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4291

2026-02-22 — Aisha Patel: Decided to prefer a two-stage approach: (1) build registry + telemetry plumbing, (2) experiment with bandit tuner. This minimizes risk to hot path. Added ENG-74182 as dependency for dashboard work.

2026-03-01 — Kelsey Rivera (SRE): Noted a potential race when registry snapshot reloads during node bootstrap. Suggested adding versioned snapshots and background reload. Marked as blocker in infra e2e until mitigation is in place.

2026-03-04 — Marco Chen: Implemented prototype bandit using Thompson Sampling with a latency-penalty term. Local test harness shows safe exploration (~3% of traffic) and quick convergence for short seqlen buckets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4337

2026-03-07 — Design review (Sana Gupta): Reviewed UI copy for 'reason' field returned to caller. Feedback: include 'confidence' and 'exploration' flags to help downstream tooling decide whether to cache routing decisions. Added to follow-up work.
